<!-- Adapt this document for the species during `index-compile-data`. It reads bottom-trawl
data from the IMR Biotic database (via BAIT) and, optionally, legacy SPD files; applies the
quantitative-catch filtering from index-template's `data-filtering.md`; removes duplicates;
computes swept-area density; and saves a compiled dataset with true zeros to data/output.
Needs a local BES database and an IMR intranet connection. Do NOT hard-wrap prose. -->

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())
```

```{r config}
source(here::here("R", "00_setup.R"))
filter_sp <- cfg$FILTER_SP          # confirm these Norwegian commonname values via BAIT taxaindex
compiled_path <- file.path(out_dir, "compiled-data.rds")
last_complete_year <- as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")) # calculate in R; DuckDB receives a numeric literal
```

## Connect to the Biotic database

Data access is provided by **BAIT** (`biotic-connect`). Connect read-only and query lazily;
`collect()` only the filtered result.

```{r connect, eval=params$recompile}
# See BAIT biotic-connect. Example:
# con    <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(Sys.getenv("BES_DATABASE_PATH")), read_only = TRUE)
# stnall <- dplyr::tbl(con, "stnall")   # station catches
# indall <- dplyr::tbl(con, "indall")   # individual / length records
```

## Station filter — make catches quantitative

Reproduce index-template `data-filtering.md` **exactly**. The `samplequality` rule is
conditional on the survey series; the `gearcondition` and `stationtype` tags are what make a
haul a valid, standardised density observation.

```{r station-filter, eval=params$recompile}
stn <- stnall |>
  dplyr::filter(
    gearcategory == "Bottom trawls",
    missiontypename %in% c("Forskningsfartøy", "Leiefartøy"),
    startyear >= cfg$FIRST_YEAR,
    startyear < last_complete_year,
    !is.na(catchweight), !is.na(distance),
    latitudestart > 0,
    gearcondition %in% 1:2,
    is.na(stationtype) | !stationtype %in% c("C", "2", "A", "E"),
    distance >= 0.3, distance <= 5
    # is.na(gear) | !gear %in% obsolete_gear_codes, # add non-missing survey-specific obsolete gear codes
    # cruiseseries %in% cfg$SURVEYS             # restrict to the chosen surveys
  ) |>
  dplyr::collect() |>
  dplyr::filter(
    dplyr::if_else(cruiseseriescode == "23", samplequality %in% 1:2, samplequality %in% 1)
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = paste(cruise, platformname, serialnumber, sep = "_"))

# Russian data are INCLUDED by default. To exclude (config INCLUDE_RUSSIAN: false):
if (!isTRUE(cfg$INCLUDE_RUSSIAN))
  stn <- dplyr::filter(stn, !nation %in% c("140", "90"))
```

## Remove duplicates

The Biotic database can contain duplicate/inconsistent records. Flag ids where the length
sample exceeds the catch, drop them, and write a report to `review/`.

```{r duplicates, eval=params$recompile}
dupe_ids <- stn |>
  dplyr::filter(commonname %in% filter_sp) |>
  dplyr::group_by(cruiseseriescode, id, commonname) |>
  dplyr::reframe(
    catchweight        = sum(catchweight, na.rm = TRUE),
    catchcount         = sum(catchcount, na.rm = TRUE),
    lengthsampleweight = sum(lengthsampleweight, na.rm = TRUE),
    lengthsamplecount  = sum(lengthsamplecount, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(catchcount < lengthsamplecount | catchweight < lengthsampleweight)

dir.create(here::here("review"), showWarnings = FALSE)
readr::write_csv(dupe_ids, here::here("review", "duplicate-station-report.csv"))
stn <- dplyr::filter(stn, !id %in% dupe_ids$id)
```

## True zeros and swept-area density

Keep stations with no catch of the target species as real zeros, then compute density. Gear
width follows `config.yaml` `GEAR_WIDTH` (see the gear-width note there).

```{r response, eval=params$recompile}
gear_width_m <- function(geartype) {
  if (identical(cfg$GEAR_WIDTH, "per_gear")) {
    dplyr::case_when(geartype == "Shrimp" ~ 25, geartype == "Cod" ~ 25 * 3.746,
                     TRUE ~ NA_real_)
  } else {
    as.numeric(cfg$GEAR_WIDTH)          # single set width; keep geartype in the model formula
  }
}

dt <- stn |>
  # join target-species catch onto the full retained-station set so absences become zeros:
  dplyr::mutate(
    biomass   = dplyr::coalesce(catchweight_sp, 0),   # <- adapt to your join of species catch
    count     = dplyr::coalesce(catchcount_sp, 0),
    gear_width = gear_width_m(geartype),
    swept_area = distance * (gear_width / 1852),        # nmi^2
    rho_biomass   = biomass / swept_area,
    rho_abundance = count   / swept_area
  )

# Fill missing/invalid bottom depth from GEBCO:
dt$depth <- ggOceanMaps::get_depth(
  dplyr::rename(dt, lon = longitudestart, lat = latitudestart),
  bathy.style = "rc", bind = FALSE
)
```

## Save

```{r save, eval=params$recompile}
saveRDS(dt, compiled_path)
```

```{r load, eval=!params$recompile}
dt <- readRDS(compiled_path)
```

## Summary

```{r summary}
dplyr::summarise(dt,
  stations = dplyr::n(),
  years    = dplyr::n_distinct(startyear),
  zeros    = mean(rho_biomass == 0)
)
```

After compiling, generate the **data report** (`{{SPECIES_SLUG}}-data-report.qmd`), then move
to Step 2 (`index-fit-model`). Record the survey list, filters, and duplicate count in
`memory/`.
